speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a limp and localized pain, but I need to ask a few more questions to narrow down the cause since there is no fever. Can you tell me if the pain is worse in the morning, at night, or only when you put weight on the leg?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the morning pain pattern is particularly important. Can you describe exactly where the pain is located on the knee, and does he feel any stiffness or swelling there? Also, has he noticed any pain in his hip or thigh?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE).

REQUEST IMAGES: Left Hip X-Ray (AP and Frog-leg lateral views).
